issue_context.title: networkd: Support `via` in BridgeFDB
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In the context of VXLAN interfaces, I cannot specify the outgoing interface for FDB entries (akin to `bridge fdb add via DEV`), which makes it hard to use IPv6 link-local addresses for VXLAN.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a parameter named `Via` or `Interface` to `[BridgeFDB]` section.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
It's possible to run the `bridge fdb add` commands manually by creating a unit that depends on the netdev, or not use link-local addresses. Neither solution fully addresses my use-case in a clean way.

maybe have two distinct functions link_remove_by_altnames() and link_remove_by_ifname() here, and then call either one or the other, or both. the boolean thing is a bit weird

hmm, why call this "update"? you use it to add only

I'd split this up into two functions: link_add_by_ifname() and link_update_by_altnames()... even if that means having the hashmap_ensure_allocated() in place twice

this doesn't look right: parsing this at the time the .network files are read might be too late. this should store the ifname as text and resolve when the fdb record is actually installed, so that this works for all network interfaces created between the time networkd reads the .network files and then finally acts on them.
Yeah, but we already use resolve_ifname() at many config parsers. We need to fix them at some point...
How does it fix ? altname or rename
Maybe, store the ifname as is in conf parsers, and then resolve it in configure_xxx().
Yeah, at that time when we parse the .network files, the corresponding netdevs may not exist yet.
But to handle such scenario is not simple. Maybe keep this as is, and leave to a later PR is ok at this time, I think. @poettering WDYT?
yes it's strange how to handle this.

if this is already a pre-existing pattern it might be Ok to merge this with the current logic, but this really should be fixed I guess. I don#t think the fix is going to be difficult: it just means storing the string the user specified and then at the time of applying things looking for the right ifindex for it. Given that networkd keeps tracks of all ifaces anyway that should be pretty easy.

the main name of an iface can chance too, and needs to be covered. if you properly encapsulate the update/removal functions as suggested, then you will get this for free, as one will remove the whole shebang including main name, and the other will register the whole shebang
the main name of the interface can change anytime too, and we should cover that here too and update the by-name hash tables, too
